$comment: Advisories accepted for now, one section per lock file (read by scripts/ci/audit.mjs, which the blocking audit job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs). Each entry maps an advisory id (GHSA-... or abandoned:<package>) to the reason it is accepted: no fixed release within the manifest ranges, not reachable, or a build or development tool only. In an npm section an entry is {"reason": ..., "via": [...]}: "via" lists the dependents the reason assumes, the packages through which npm audit reports the vulnerable package (its "effects"), and "(direct)" if the project itself depends on it. The audit fails when the advisory is reported through a dependent the entry does not list, so the reason is checked again before the list grows. A composer entry is the reason alone: composer audit names no dependents. Fix an advisory with a compatible update first; list it here only when that is not possible. The audit fails on an advisory that is not listed and on an entry or a dependent that no longer matches one, so an entry is removed as soon as its fix lands.

GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv.reason: node-forge (high). No fixed release: every node-forge version is affected and 1.4.0, the newest, is locked. Build and development tool only: it comes in through the Expo CLI (expo -> @expo/cli and @expo/code-signing-certificates), which runs on the developer's or build machine to sign development manifests and read iOS signing identities. It is not in the Android or iOS app bundle (checked with the exported source maps), and neither server loads it.

GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr.reason: decode-uri-component (moderate). No fixed release within the manifest ranges: expo-router ~57.0.23 (newest 57.0.24) needs query-string ^7.1.3 (newest 7.x is 7.1.3), which needs decode-uri-component ^0.2.2; npm's only offered fix is a breaking expo-router downgrade. The package is in the app bundle, but expo-router parses incoming links with its own parser (URLSearchParams in its getStateFromPath fork); query-string's parse, the only caller of decode-uri-component, is React Navigation's default getStateFromPath, which expo-router replaces in its linking config. If it were reached, a crafted link could slow the app on the device that opens it; no server uses this package. Remove this entry with the Expo update that drops it (the audit then reports it as stale).

GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq.reason: uuid (moderate). No fixed release within the manifest ranges: uuid 7.0.3 comes from xcode 3.0.1 (^7.0.3; 3.0.1 is the newest xcode), which @expo/config-plugins 57 requires (^3.0.1). Not reachable: the flaw needs a caller-supplied output buffer for v3, v5 or v6, and xcode only calls uuid.v4() without one (xcode/lib/pbxProject.js). Build tool only: xcode edits the iOS project during prebuild on the developer's or build machine; uuid is not in the Android or iOS app bundle.
